findings.title: Built-in TLS pins for vendor hosts are never enforced unless the host is also listed in pin_hosts, which is empty by default
findings.source: Any TLS server presenting a certificate for api.anthropic.com, chatgpt.com, auth.openai.com, openrouter.ai, management-api.x.ai and similar hosts. Pinning turns on only when cfg.security.pinHosts is non-empty (AppEnvironment.swift:30). pinHosts defaults to [] (AppConfig.swift:106/119), and the shipped config.toml leaves the line commented out (ConfigLoader.swift:312).
findings.sink: PinningDelegate.swift:36-44 passes any host missing from pinnedHosts to .performDefaultHandling (system trust only). PinBaseline.pin(for:) is only reached at line 63, after that guard. On top of that, HTTPClient.pinned returns an unpinned HTTPClient() when pinnedHosts is empty (HTTPClient.swift:39-40).
findings.description: PinBaseline's own comment says it closes the first-connection window for every vendor host. The settings UI tells users 'Baseline pins for known vendor hosts ship in-binary — leave empty unless you have a private endpoint.' In the code, though, a baseline pin is only checked for hosts that are already in the user-supplied pinnedHosts set, and with the default empty list no delegate is installed at all. OAuth bearer tokens and API keys are therefore protected only by system trust, while the product says pinning is on.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) The attacker gets a root CA trusted on the victim's Mac: a corporate TLS-inspection proxy, malware-installed root, MDM profile, or a CA mis-issuance for a vendor domain. 2) The victim runs ai-taskbar with the default config and follows the UI advice to leave pin_hosts empty. 3) The attacker intercepts the refresh to api.anthropic.com or chatgpt.com. System trust accepts the forged leaf and no SPKI check runs. 4) The attacker captures the Authorization: Bearer OAuth access token (and, when manage_oauth_refresh=true, the refresh token sent to platform.claude.com or auth.openai.com), which gives access to the user's Claude/ChatGPT account.
preconditions: Attacker-controlled certificate that the victim's system trusts (rogue or corporate root CA, or mis-issuance)
Default config (pin_hosts empty), which the settings UI recommends
findings.impact: Theft of vendor OAuth/API credentials by an on-path attacker that the shipped baseline pins were meant to stop. This is a defense-in-depth failure made worse because users are told the protection is active.
findings.fix: Always install PinningDelegate, and make the effective pin set Set(PinBaseline.baselineHosts.keys) ∪ pin_hosts. HTTPClient.pinned should return a pinned session even when pin_hosts is empty, and the host check should be pinnedHosts.contains(host) || PinBaseline.pin(for: host) != nil. If the current behavior is intentional, correct the UI strings and the PinBaseline doc comment instead.
findings.evidence: AppEnvironment.swift:30-37: `if !cfg.security.pinHosts.isEmpty { http = try HTTPClient.pinned(...) } else { http = HTTPClient() }`. HTTPClient.swift:39-40: `guard !pinnedHosts.isEmpty else { return HTTPClient() }`. PinningDelegate.swift:36: the membership check runs before PinBaseline.pin(for:) at line 63. en.lproj/Localizable.strings:153/210 claim baseline pins ship in the binary and advise leaving the field empty.
